summary.oneLiner: Lloyds Metals executed a historic scale-up in FY26 with iron ore production doubling to 22MT and pellet capacity hitting 8MT, driving standalone EBITDA margins to ~34% via structural logistics savings. The strategic pivot into critical minerals via DRC copper/cobalt assets (Surya + CHEMAF) and the impending BHQ beneficiation plant position the company as a diversified energy-transition play beyond traditional steel inputs.
summary.business: LMEL mines high-grade hematite iron ore at its Surjagarh Iron Ore Mine (SIOM) in Maharashtra and converts a growing share of it into value-added products - sponge iron (DRI), iron ore pellets and captive power - through its Ghugus and Konsari facilities. The Company operates two business segments, Mining and Value Added Products, and is extending its integrated model internationally through stakes in copper-cobalt assets in the Democratic Republic of Congo and through its mine-development-operator (MDO) subsidiary, Thriveni.

Mining: Iron ore (Direct Shipping Ore and Banded Hematite Quartzite)

endMarkets: Indian steel industry / domestic demand for iron ore and pellets|Global copper-cobalt value chain via DRC operations|Vidarbha / Maharashtra regional industrial ecosystem

currentContext.strengths: High-grade hematite ore (~63% Fe average) with mining lease valid until CY2057 and a zero-premium payment obligation to the Government of Maharashtra for the entire lease period - a structural cost advantage versus competitors facing re-auction at higher premiums|Large geological resource base of 863 million tonnes (157 MnT DSO + 706 MnT BHQ) supporting mine life well beyond CY2030, when more than 80 MTPA of competing industry capacity is expected to come up for re-auction|Genuinely end-to-end integrated ferrous value chain (captive mining through beneficiation, pelletisation, DRI, captive power, slurry pipeline logistics) that eliminates external raw-material dependencies and reduces exposure to intermediate product price cycles|Rapid step-up in value-added product (VAP) share: VAP contributed 32% of standalone revenue and 30% of standalone EBIT in FY26, up from 20% of revenue and 11% of EBIT in FY25|85 km Hedri-Konsari slurry pipeline lowering logistics cost and reducing dependence on road transport for ore evacuation|Annuity-like earnings stability from the MDO (Mine Development and Operations) subsidiary Thriveni, which operates on long-tenure, fee-based contracts with blue-chip clients, insulated from commodity price movements|Proven execution track record: pellet plant, DRI units and the slurry pipeline were each commissioned ahead of or on schedule, with the first pellet plant completed in 16 months and reaching 100% utilisation within 4 months
currentContext.strategies: Scale Capacity Expansion - pursuing a phased capacity expansion programme spanning mining, beneficiation, pellets, integrated steel and copper, executed through disciplined planning and standardised project delivery to build a larger, more efficient operating base.|End-to-End Value Integration - transforming from an iron-ore-only miner into a fully integrated metals and mining enterprise across beneficiation, pelletisation, steel manufacturing and copper, reducing dependence on a single revenue stream and improving cost control, margin stability and supply security.|Diversified Resource Portfolio - broadening the resource base beyond iron ore through entry into copper and cobalt and recurring Mine Development and Operations (MDO) contracts, reducing concentration risk and creating multiple growth engines.|Logistics Cost Optimisation - redesigning the logistics network (principally slurry pipelines) to reduce structural freight costs, dependence on road transport, weather-related disruptions and carbon emissions, while supporting higher production volumes.|Sustainable Operations Integration - embedding sustainability into strategic and operational decisions via equipment electrification, renewable power, slurry pipelines and waste-to-energy systems to lower emissions while improving productivity.|Global critical-minerals diversification - entry into copper marks a step towards a future-ready portfolio aligned with global electrification and decarbonisation trends, participating in growing demand for critical minerals as a resource provider.|MDO annuity-earnings strategy - leveraging Mine Developer and Operator engagements (through subsidiary Thriveni) for stable, annuity-like revenues that reduce overall portfolio cyclicality and align with India's focus on domestic coal production and energy security.|Dividend decisions are governed by a formal Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The Board determines dividend for a period after considering the Company's financial performance, advice of Executive Management, and stated capital allocation plans - including expected cash requirements for working capital, capital expenditure in technology and infrastructure, general corporate purposes, and investments required towards execution of the Company's strategy - balancing shareholder distribution against reinvestment needs. For FY26 the AGM notice records a resolution to declare a dividend of Rs 1 per equity share of face value Rs 1.
currentContext.expansion: LMEL is executing a multi-year forward-integration programme, transitioning from a merchant iron ore miner to an integrated, low-cost steel producer via a phased programme spanning BHQ beneficiation, large-scale pelletisation, expanded DRI manufacturing and eventual long/flat steel capacity. Completed in FY26: the 85 km Hedri-Konsari slurry pipeline (Line 1, 10 MTPA) fully operational; the first 4 MTPA Pellet Plant (Plant 1) at Konsari, commissioned and completed in 16 months from construction start, reaching 100% annualised capacity utilisation within four months; and the 360 KTPA DRI expansion at Ghugus, commissioned in Q2 FY26. A second 4 MTPA pellet plant at Konsari (Plant 2) was commissioned in May 2026, just after FY26 close. Under construction/planned: a 1.2 Million Tonne Wire Rod, Blast Furnace and Coke Oven integrated steel plant (board-approved October 2023 and January 2024) comprising a sponge iron plant (2x500 TPD), captive power plant, EAF-based SMS (2x50T), ladle refining furnaces (2x50T), a vacuum degassing unit (1x50T), an RHF (120 TPH), a wire rod mill (2x600,000 TPA) a blast furnace (840,000 TPA) and a coke oven (400,000 TPA) - construction has commenced and the project is at an advanced stage; a third 4 MTPA pellet plant (Plant 3) and associated slurry pipeline at Ghugus, with land procured and Environmental Clearance in hand, construction commenced in Q4 FY26 and commissioning expected in FY27; and a parallel 195 km slurry pipeline under development that will add ~16 MTPA of evacuation capacity (taking total pipeline evacuation capacity to ~26 MTPA) and extend the network to Chandrapur. Separately, the Company is diversifying into critical minerals through a 50% stake in the operational Surya Mines platform and a 49% stake in the Chemaf Group, both in the DRC, targeting a combined pathway to ~100,000 TPA copper and ~20,000 TPA cobalt capacity, and is scaling its MDO subsidiary (Thriveni) into new mineral categories (coal, copper, bauxite) and international contracts. FY24-FY26 cumulative capital expenditure was stated in the narrative as part of this programme (rupee quantum not reproduced here; see NAMED DISCLOSURE handling).
currentContext.mdna: Domestic steel demand is expected to remain infrastructure-led, supported by the Government of India's long-term capacity targets of 300 million tonnes by 2030 and 500 million tonnes by 2047, though capacity utilisation across the industry will depend on the pace of demand absorption.|The Company expects to benefit from rising domestic steel demand and a global upcycle in iron ore, supported by its strong resource base and expanding mining capacities.|Global refined copper consumption is projected to grow to 28.66 million tonnes in 2026 and 29.24 million tonnes in 2027 (International Copper Study Group), driven by electrification, renewable energy, EVs and data centres - a structural demand tailwind cited in support of the Company's copper diversification.|India's coal sector is expected to sustain strong production growth toward 1.15 billion tonnes, reinforcing energy security and supporting stable, annuity-like MDO revenue for the Company.|Forward integration into beneficiation, pelletisation, DRI and steel is expected to enable value capture across the entire chain, enhancing margins and reducing exposure to commodity price volatility, aided by logistics investments such as slurry pipelines that strengthen cost competitiveness and supply reliability.|The Company has been named a preferred partner for the Panguna mine in Bougainville, Papua New Guinea, and is advancing community-focused initiatives there, including a proposed 100-bedded hospital, alongside this opportunity.|Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) engagements, conducted through subsidiary Thriveni, provide stable, annuity-like revenues under long-tenure, fee-based contracts across India and internationally.

risks.risk: Global steel demand and commodity-cycle exposure
risks.note: Management flags global steel demand dynamics, economic slowdown and market volatility as key risks facing the Company, given its revenue base is still weighted to iron ore and steel-linked products.

risks.risk: Rising finance costs and increasing leverage
risks.note: Management explicitly flags rising finance costs as a key risk. The FY26 Key Financial Ratios disclosure shows Debt-Equity Ratio rising to 0.47x from 0.16x (+201% YoY) on increased borrowings, Current Ratio falling to 0.87x from 1.62x (-46%) on higher current liabilities, and Debt-Service Coverage Ratio falling to 1.35x from 8.37x (-84%), consistent with the Company funding a large capex programme partly through debt.
The Company flags potential constraints or significant increases in raw material prices as a key risk to profitability.

risks.risk: Regulatory and approval delays / policy risk
risks.note: Operations, ongoing projects and profitability may be impacted by delays in government approvals and procedural processes, or unfavourable changes in government policy relating to mining, allocations and tariffs.

risks.risk: Labour law, safety and workforce risk
risks.note: The mining and steel industries operate under stringent labour and health-and-safety regulations; any safety lapse could damage property, assets and human capital, and labour shortages could adversely impact operations and ongoing projects.
Rising environmental concerns and regulatory requirements relating to carbon emissions and water availability may impose operational constraints that could impact the Company's growth trajectory.

risks.risk: Social licence to operate / regional unrest risk
risks.note: The Company operates in a socio-economically sensitive region (Gadchiroli/Chandrapur, Maharashtra); any unrest in the region could adversely affect mining operations.

one-line thesis: Lloyds Metals executed a historic scale-up in FY26 with iron ore production doubling to 22MT and pellet capacity hitting 8MT, driving standalone EBITDA margins to ~34% via structural logistics savings. The strategic pivot into critical minerals via DRC copper/cobalt assets (Surya + CHEMAF) and the impending BHQ beneficiation plant position the company as a diversified energy-transition play beyond traditional steel inputs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 17,000 Cr consolidated (INR 13,838 Cr standalone, +104% YoY); EBITDA/Margin: INR 4,673 Cr standalone (+133% YoY), margin expanded 418 bps to 33.77% (structural, not one-off); PAT: INR 3,829 Cr consolidated (+120% YoY standalone to INR 3,194 Cr); Order Book: N/A (Mining/Production driven), but secured take-or-pay pipeline contract with Tata Steel; Net Debt: INR 3,901 Cr standalone (manageable, ~1-1.5x EBITDA target), consolidation includes Thriveni debt (RPS redemption ongoing). One-offs: None material; margin expansion driven by value-added mix (pellets/DRI) and slurry pipeline commissioning.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Topline to scale with volume (Iron ore dispatch 27MT, Pellets 7.75-8MT in FY27); Margin: Structural sustainment >30% aided by INR 2,000 Cr annualized cost savings by FY28; Order Inflow: New mining leases in Odisha/Jharkhand commencing FY27; Capex/Commissioning: FY27 capex ~INR 15,000 Cr consolidated (INR 10,500 Cr standalone + INR 2,000 Cr Copper + Thriveni); Wire rod mill commissioning late FY26; BHQ plant phase-1 ready by Dec 2027.
order book & pipeline: Production-driven model; Key contractual anchor: Take-or-pay slurry pipeline agreement with Tata Steel ensuring high free cash flow conversion; Mining lease expansions in Gadchiroli (55MT capacity) and new Odisha/Jharkhand mines targeting 35MT+ iron ore volume in FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail: Iron Ore: Production 22MT (+120% YoY), Sales 16.18MT, Realization INR 5,806/ton, EBITDA/ton INR 1,930. Pellets: 3.03MT produced in FY26 (ramped to 100% utilization in 4 months), Realization INR 9,590/ton, EBITDA/ton INR 4,040. DRI: 480k tons (+56% YoY), Realization INR 27,306/ton. Thriveni (Coal/Iron): EBITDA INR 1,990 Cr (+87% YoY), Margin 25%. Copper (DRC): 700-750 tons produced in Q4, targeting 9-10k tons in FY27 from Surya; CHEMAF to contribute from July 2027.
growth verticals / optionality: BHQ Beneficiation Plant (Dec 2027): Converts low-grade ore to 66-67% grade, reducing royalty costs and boosting EBITDA/ton by INR 700-800. Steel Integration: 1.2MT wire rod mill commissioning late FY26. Critical Minerals: Pathway to 100k tons copper capacity over 3-5 years via CHEMAF/Surya. Logistics: Second slurry pipeline (Hedri-Ghugus) to save INR 500/ton on 16MT volume.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin sustained at ~34% due to value-added mix shift (32% of revenue vs 20% prior) and operational leverage. Cost deflation: Slurry pipeline and EV/LNG mining fleet driving INR 2,000 Cr annualized savings by FY28. BHQ project expected to further reduce cost base via royalty arbitrage on lower-grade feed.
capex / expansion: Total FY24-26 spend: INR 13,500 Cr. FY27 Guidance: ~INR 15,000 Cr consolidated (INR 10,500 Cr standalone for BHQ/Steel/Pellets; ~INR 2,000 Cr for Copper completion; ~INR 1,000 Cr Thriveni). Funding: Primarily internal accruals + debt (target 1-1.5x Net Debt/EBITDA); no equity dilution planned for parent.
capital allocation: Debt reduction: Redeeming Thriveni RPS (INR 700 Cr paid April 2026, remaining INR 2,100 Cr over 3 years). Reinvestment: Heavy capex into vertical integration (Steel, BHQ) and critical minerals (DRC). Potential future IPO for Thriveni subsidiary to unlock value, though not immediate.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical/Operational Risk: DRC operations (mitigated by US strategic partnership); Execution Risk: BHQ plant commissioning by Dec 2027; Commodity Price Volatility: Iron ore/pellet realization sensitivity; Regulatory: Royalty changes on low-grade ore (managed via beneficiation).
management quality / tone: Highly confident, execution-focused, and visionary. Emphasizes 'structural' margin improvements over cyclical gains. Strong emphasis on strategic alignment with US critical mineral goals to de-risk DRC exposure. Celebratory of market cap milestone (INR 1 Lakh Cr).
non-obvious takeaways: The US-DRC critical mineral agreement (Dec 2025) is a key de-risking factor for their Congo assets, positioning Lloyds as a non-Chinese alternative for US supply chains. The take-or-pay nature of the Tata Steel pipeline asset generates disproportionate free cash flow relative to sustaining capex. BHQ beneficiation not just a volume play but a significant royalty tax arbitrage.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain diversification away from China for critical minerals | US Defense & EV OEMs | beneficiary | High | Lloyds' DRC assets (Surya/CHEMAF) are explicitly framed as a flagship project under the new US-DRC critical mineral pact, offering a secure, non-Chinese source of copper/cobalt. |
| High logistics costs in Indian steel production | Tata Steel | beneficiary | High | Beneficiary of the dedicated, cost-efficient slurry pipeline near Kalinganagar, securing stable iron ore/pellet supply with reduced transport costs. |
| Margin compression in low-grade iron ore mining | Competitors without beneficiation tech | loser | Med | Lloyds' BHQ plant allows profitable processing of low-grade ore (royalty arbitrage), potentially squeezing out players reliant on high-grade reserves or lacking beneficiation tech. |

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Iron Ore: Production 22MT (+120% YoY), Sales 16.18MT, Realization INR 5,806/ton, EBITDA/ton INR 1,930. Pellets: 3.03MT produced in FY26 (ramped to 100% utilization in 4 months), Realization INR 9,590/ton, EBITDA/ton INR 4,040. DRI: 480k tons (+56% YoY), Realization INR 27,306/ton. Thriveni (Coal/Iron): EBITDA INR 1,990 Cr (+87% YoY), Margin 25%. Copper (DRC): 700-750 tons produced in Q4, targeting 9-10k tons in FY27 from Surya; CHEMAF to contribute from July 2027.

products.body:
- **Mining:** Iron ore (Direct Shipping Ore and Banded Hematite Quartzite)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Production-driven model; Key contractual anchor: Take-or-pay slurry pipeline agreement with Tata Steel ensuring high free cash flow conversion; Mining lease expansions in Gadchiroli (55MT capacity) and new Odisha/Jharkhand mines targeting 35MT+ iron ore volume in FY27.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Topline to scale with volume (Iron ore dispatch 27MT, Pellets 7.75-8MT in FY27); Margin: Structural sustainment >30% aided by INR 2,000 Cr annualized cost savings by FY28; Order Inflow: New mining leases in Odisha/Jharkhand commencing FY27; Capex/Commissioning: FY27 capex ~INR 15,000 Cr consolidated (INR 10,500 Cr standalone + INR 2,000 Cr Copper + Thriveni); Wire rod mill commissioning late FY26; BHQ plant phase-1 ready by Dec 2027.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: BHQ Beneficiation Plant (Dec 2027): Converts low-grade ore to 66-67% grade, reducing royalty costs and boosting EBITDA/ton by INR 700-800. Steel Integration: 1.2MT wire rod mill commissioning late FY26. Critical Minerals: Pathway to 100k tons copper capacity over 3-5 years via CHEMAF/Surya. Logistics: Second slurry pipeline (Hedri-Ghugus) to save INR 500/ton on 16MT volume.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic steel demand is expected to remain infrastructure-led, supported by the Government of India's long-term capacity targets of 300 million tonnes by 2030 and 500 million tonnes by 2047, though capacity utilisation across the industry will depend on the pace of demand absorption.
- The Company expects to benefit from rising domestic steel demand and a global upcycle in iron ore, supported by its strong resource base and expanding mining capacities.
- Global refined copper consumption is projected to grow to 28.66 million tonnes in 2026 and 29.24 million tonnes in 2027 (International Copper Study Group), driven by electrification, renewable energy, EVs and data centres - a structural demand tailwind cited in support of the Company's copper diversification.
- India's coal sector is expected to sustain strong production growth toward 1.15 billion tonnes, reinforcing energy security and supporting stable, annuity-like MDO revenue for the Company.
- Forward integration into beneficiation, pelletisation, DRI and steel is expected to enable value capture across the entire chain, enhancing margins and reducing exposure to commodity price volatility, aided by logistics investments such as slurry pipelines that strengthen cost competitiveness and supply reliability.
- The Company has been named a preferred partner for the Panguna mine in Bougainville, Papua New Guinea, and is advancing community-focused initiatives there, including a proposed 100-bedded hospital, alongside this opportunity.
- Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) engagements, conducted through subsidiary Thriveni, provide stable, annuity-like revenues under long-tenure, fee-based contracts across India and internationally.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin sustained at ~34% due to value-added mix shift (32% of revenue vs 20% prior) and operational leverage. Cost deflation: Slurry pipeline and EV/LNG mining fleet driving INR 2,000 Cr annualized savings by FY28. BHQ project expected to further reduce cost base via royalty arbitrage on lower-grade feed.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt reduction: Redeeming Thriveni RPS (INR 700 Cr paid April 2026, remaining INR 2,100 Cr over 3 years). Reinvestment: Heavy capex into vertical integration (Steel, BHQ) and critical minerals (DRC). Potential future IPO for Thriveni subsidiary to unlock value, though not immediate.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: LMEL is executing a multi-year forward-integration programme, transitioning from a merchant iron ore miner to an integrated, low-cost steel producer via a phased programme spanning BHQ beneficiation, large-scale pelletisation, expanded DRI manufacturing and eventual long/flat steel capacity. Completed in FY26: the 85 km Hedri-Konsari slurry pipeline (Line 1, 10 MTPA) fully operational; the first 4 MTPA Pellet Plant (Plant 1) at Konsari, commissioned and completed in 16 months from construction start, reaching 100% annualised capacity utilisation within four months; and the 360 KTPA DRI expansion at Ghugus, commissioned in Q2 FY26. A second 4 MTPA pellet plant at Konsari (Plant 2) was commissioned in May 2026, just after FY26 close. Under construction/planned: a 1.2 Million Tonne Wire Rod, Blast Furnace and Coke Oven integrated steel plant (board-approved October 2023 and January 2024) comprising a sponge iron plant (2x500 TPD), captive power plant, EAF-based SMS (2x50T), ladle refining furnaces (2x50T), a vacuum degassing unit (1x50T), an RHF (120 TPH), a wire rod mill (2x600,000 TPA) a blast furnace (840,000 TPA) and a coke oven (400,000 TPA) - construction has commenced and the project is at an advanced stage; a third 4 MTPA pellet plant (Plant 3) and associated slurry pipeline at Ghugus, with land procured and Environmental Clearance in hand, construction commenced in Q4 FY26 and commissioning expected in FY27; and a parallel 195 km slurry pipeline under development that will add ~16 MTPA of evacuation capacity (taking total pipeline evacuation capacity to ~26 MTPA) and extend the network to Chandrapur. Separately, the Company is diversifying into critical minerals through a 50% stake in the operational Surya Mines platform and a 49% stake in the Chemaf Group, both in the DRC, targeting a combined pathway to ~100,000 TPA copper and ~20,000 TPA cobalt capacity, and is scaling its MDO subsidiary (Thriveni) into new mineral categories (coal, copper, bauxite) and international contracts. FY24-FY26 cumulative capital expenditure was stated in the narrative as part of this programme (rupee quantum not reproduced here; see NAMED DISCLOSURE handling).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, execution-focused, and visionary. Emphasizes 'structural' margin improvements over cyclical gains. Strong emphasis on strategic alignment with US critical mineral goals to de-risk DRC exposure. Celebratory of market cap milestone (INR 1 Lakh Cr).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- High-grade hematite ore (~63% Fe average) with mining lease valid until CY2057 and a zero-premium payment obligation to the Government of Maharashtra for the entire lease period - a structural cost advantage versus competitors facing re-auction at higher premiums
- Large geological resource base of 863 million tonnes (157 MnT DSO + 706 MnT BHQ) supporting mine life well beyond CY2030, when more than 80 MTPA of competing industry capacity is expected to come up for re-auction
- Genuinely end-to-end integrated ferrous value chain (captive mining through beneficiation, pelletisation, DRI, captive power, slurry pipeline logistics) that eliminates external raw-material dependencies and reduces exposure to intermediate product price cycles
- Rapid step-up in value-added product (VAP) share: VAP contributed 32% of standalone revenue and 30% of standalone EBIT in FY26, up from 20% of revenue and 11% of EBIT in FY25
- 85 km Hedri-Konsari slurry pipeline lowering logistics cost and reducing dependence on road transport for ore evacuation
- Annuity-like earnings stability from the MDO (Mine Development and Operations) subsidiary Thriveni, which operates on long-tenure, fee-based contracts with blue-chip clients, insulated from commodity price movements
- Proven execution track record: pellet plant, DRI units and the slurry pipeline were each commissioned ahead of or on schedule, with the first pellet plant completed in 16 months and reaching 100% utilisation within 4 months

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical/Operational Risk: DRC operations (mitigated by US strategic partnership); Execution Risk: BHQ plant commissioning by Dec 2027; Commodity Price Volatility: Iron ore/pellet realization sensitivity; Regulatory: Royalty changes on low-grade ore (managed via beneficiation).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The US-DRC critical mineral agreement (Dec 2025) is a key de-risking factor for their Congo assets, positioning Lloyds as a non-Chinese alternative for US supply chains. The take-or-pay nature of the Tata Steel pipeline asset generates disproportionate free cash flow relative to sustaining capex. BHQ beneficiation not just a volume play but a significant royalty tax arbitrage.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain diversification away from China for critical minerals | US Defense & EV OEMs | beneficiary | High | Lloyds' DRC assets (Surya/CHEMAF) are explicitly framed as a flagship project under the new US-DRC critical mineral pact, offering a secure, non-Chinese source of copper/cobalt. |
| High logistics costs in Indian steel production | Tata Steel | beneficiary | High | Beneficiary of the dedicated, cost-efficient slurry pipeline near Kalinganagar, securing stable iron ore/pellet supply with reduced transport costs. |
| Margin compression in low-grade iron ore mining | Competitors without beneficiation tech | loser | Med | Lloyds' BHQ plant allows profitable processing of low-grade ore (royalty arbitrage), potentially squeezing out players reliant on high-grade reserves or lacking beneficiation tech. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Tata Steel / BRPL] Tata Steel - Lloyds Metals MoU to explore strategic collaboration across mining, logistics and steel manufacturing; BRPL began MDO operations at Tata Steel's Joda West manganese mines on 1 June 2026 (Q1FY27 EBITDA INR ~48 Cr, pellet production 540 KTPA) and a feasibility study for a slurry pipeline linking Tata Steel's Odisha mines to its steel plants is under discussion, to be developed by BRPL under a BOT service model.
- [Panguna, via Thriveni/associate] Mining lease commencement with the ABG on 7 August; 400+ people employed with 1,200+ engaged; Learning & Development Centre inaugurated 11 July with 300 cadets; hospital construction to complete in 6 months; exploration drilling started to validate historical geology.
- [Geomysore gold] Described as India's first private integrated gold mining and processing company; plant inaugurated by the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on 24 July 2026; Q1 production of ROM 0.17 MT and exploration/drilling of 14,105 mtr.
- [Copper loss driver] Q1FY27 copper EBITDA was negative $2.63 mn, which the deck attributes to the closure of EP1 (lower revenue), higher sulphuric acid and diesel prices "due to middle east war", and continuing employee and operating costs during the transition.
- [Thriveni coal recognition] Thriveni Sainik Mining PB West and PB North West achieved a 5-Star Rating from the Ministry of Coal (FY2024-25) and retained the No. 1 position among all opencast coal mines in India for a 2nd consecutive year.
